serverEvents.title: Server-to-client events (SSE `data:`), added by the stream compiler

answer.purpose: The one-line direct answer, big and first.
answer.useWhen: Almost every UI answer starts with one. A yes/no, a number, a verdict.
answer.streaming: Streams word by word (phrases 150 ms apart).

example.text: Yes — you can afford the trip if you skip one dinner out a week.
example.detail: Based on the $3,200 budget you gave me.

text.purpose: Markdown prose (bold, italics, links, inline code). No raw HTML.
text.useWhen: Explanations, context, anything that reads best as sentences.
text.streaming: Streams word by word; markdown is re-parsed each frame, open ** is closed automatically.

example.md: A **bone-in leg** is forgiving and easy to carve. Rest it 30 minutes so the oven is free for potatoes.

heading.useWhen: Break a long answer into 2–5 parts.
heading.streaming: Appears when the line is complete (short).

note.purpose: Callout box: tip, warning, safety note.
note.useWhen: One important caveat the user must not miss. Max 2 per answer.

example.label: Food safety
example.text: USDA recommends 145°F internal temperature plus a 3-minute rest for whole cuts of lamb.

list.purpose: Bulleted or numbered list; optional columns (a light table).
list.useWhen: 3–12 parallel items. Use table if more than 3 columns.
list.streaming: Rows draw in 110 ms apart as each item finishes.

steps.purpose: Numbered how-to steps with optional time and detail.
steps.streaming: Each step appears when complete; rows 110 ms apart.

items.title: Roast in hot fat until deep gold

table.useWhen: Data with 3+ columns or more than 6 rows. Numbers right-aligned.
table.streaming: Header first, then rows 110 ms apart.

facts.useWhen: Key facts about one thing: a place, product, plan.

brief.purpose: Short briefing: title, bullets, optional people.

number.purpose: One big metric with delta and sparkline.
number.useWhen: A single number is the answer (revenue, ETA, total).
number.streaming: Counts up over 750 ms (ease-out cubic); sparkline draws 600 ms.

chart.purpose: Bar, line, area, pie/donut, scatter. Data inline or by $ref to a tool result.
chart.useWhen: Trends, shares, distributions. Never for fewer than 3 points. $calcSeries makes a live chart from state.
chart.streaming: Axes appear first; series draw over 900 ms once the data array is complete.

comparison.purpose: Side-by-side options with rows of attributes, a winner and pros/cons.
comparison.useWhen: 2–4 options the user is choosing between.
comparison.streaming: Column headers first, then attribute rows 110 ms apart; 'best pick' badge last.

agenda.purpose: Time-ordered items: schedule, itinerary, cooking timeline.
agenda.useWhen: Anything with clock times or dates in order.
agenda.streaming: Rows 110 ms apart; 'next' item pulses once.

progress.purpose: Multi-step status of the agent's own work.
progress.useWhen: Long jobs (searching, booking, building a tool). Also shows while 'working'.
progress.streaming: Active step shimmers; each change plays the quiet tick.

image.purpose: One image. The model writes a search query or an asset id; the server resolves the real URL.
image.useWhen: When seeing it helps (a dish, a place, a part). Never decorative filler.
image.streaming: Placeholder with the right aspect ratio at once; image fades in 280 ms when the server patches the URL.

example.query: slow roasted rosemary garlic leg of lamb on carving board

gallery.purpose: Grid or carousel of images (moodboard, options, steps).
gallery.useWhen: 3–12 images the user compares or browses.
gallery.streaming: Tiles appear with placeholders 110 ms apart; each fades in when resolved.

map.purpose: Interactive map with pins and an optional route.
map.useWhen: Places, road trips, 'near me'. Coordinates come from a geocoding tool, not the model's memory.
map.streaming: Tiles load first; pins drop 110 ms apart; route draws 900 ms.

diagram.purpose: Nodes-and-arrows diagram, or a labelled picture with tappable hotspots.
diagram.useWhen: How parts connect (bike systems, a process, an org chart).
diagram.streaming: Nodes pop in 110 ms apart in layout order; edges draw 400 ms after both ends exist.

sources.useWhen: Any answer that used the web or user documents.
sources.streaming: Chips slide in at the end.

buttons.purpose: A row of action buttons (follow-ups, open, copy).
buttons.useWhen: End of an answer: 2–3 next steps. Max 4 buttons.

items.label: Adjust for 5 guests
items.text: Adjust the lamb roast plan for 5 guests

choices.purpose: Tappable chips to answer a question quickly (single or multi select).
choices.useWhen: When you need one missing fact before answering well.

form.purpose: A small form; submitting sends one follow-up message (or calls a tool) with the values.
form.useWhen: Collecting 2–6 inputs (booking, a brief, a filter).
form.streaming: Fields appear 110 ms apart; submit enables when required fields are filled.

submit.label: Find tables
submit.text: Find a table on {date} for {size} people

control.purpose: A live input bound to a state variable: slider, stepper, toggle, segmented, select.
control.useWhen: Calculators and 'what if' explorers. Changing it never calls the model.
control.streaming: Appears when complete; values update at 60 fps locally.

result.purpose: A computed read-out: label + value from a safe formula over state.
result.useWhen: Pairs with control: totals, per-person shares, projections.
result.streaming: Number rolls to each new value in 250 ms (750 ms on first show).

todo.purpose: Checklist the user can tick (state is kept locally and can sync back).
todo.useWhen: Shopping lists, packing lists, 'what needs me'.
todo.streaming: Rows 110 ms apart; ticking plays a soft tick.

tabs.purpose: Tabs; children point here with parent + slot.
tabs.useWhen: 2–6 views of the same thing (Frame / Wheels / Brakes).
tabs.streaming: Tab strip appears first; the first tab's content streams; others fill in the background.

person.purpose: Contact card: name, role, org, facts.
person.useWhen: Who-is questions, attendees, a contact to email.

email.purpose: Draft email the user can edit and send (send always needs approval).
email.streaming: Subject first; body streams as phrases.

example.subject: Re: renewal
example.body: Hi Mira — Thursday works. I'll bring the SSO timeline.

approval.purpose: Ask before an action with side effects. Sets card status to needs-you.
approval.useWhen: Before sending, booking, paying, deleting, posting.
approval.streaming: Drops in with the needs-you sound; buttons are disabled for 400 ms to stop accidental taps.

created.purpose: Receipt for something made (event, doc, file, reservation).
created.streaming: Pops with the 'sent' sound; shows Undo for 10 s if reversible.

connect.purpose: Ask the user to connect an account (OAuth).
connect.useWhen: A tool needs access the user hasn't granted.

error.purpose: A friendly failure with a fix or retry.
error.useWhen: Tool failed, offline, timed out, invalid output after repair.
error.streaming: Plays error sound once; card status becomes error.

example.title: The flight search took too long

columns.purpose: 2–3 columns; children point here with parent + slot (0,1,2).
columns.useWhen: Image beside text, two short lists side by side. Collapses to one column under 520 px.
columns.streaming: Column frames appear at once; children stream into them.

section.purpose: A titled group, optionally collapsible; children point here with parent.
section.useWhen: Grouping related blocks in long answers.

app.purpose: A generated mini-tool (HTML+CSS+JS) that runs in a locked-down sandboxed iframe. See section 7.
app.useWhen: Only when no mix of native components can do it: a game, a drawing pad, a sound toy, a bespoke simulator.
app.streaming: Shows a 'Building…' frame at the declared height; mounts once the whole source has arrived and passed checks.

alert.purpose: A proactive alert that drops out of the notch (title + one line + up to 2 actions). Opens the island to the bar or open state.
alert.useWhen: Something needs the user without being asked: a renewal at risk, a meeting moved, research finished.
alert.streaming: Shape morphs first (arrival spring), then title, then detail 150 ms later; actions fade in last.

example.title: Northwind may not renew
example.detail: Renews in 9 days · their champion left

glance.purpose: A one-line read-out that lives inside the notch bar (icon, text, optional value).
glance.useWhen: Short status the user can read at a glance: 'Northwind · Needs you', 'Researching · 18 sources'.
glance.streaming: Crossfades in place (240 ms); never animates width more than once per 560 ms.

receipt.purpose: The done-line shown in the bar after an action (≤ 80 chars), with optional Undo.
receipt.useWhen: Right after a side effect succeeds or fails: 'Sent to Tomás · Thursday 10:00 held ✓'.
receipt.streaming: Bar morphs to receipt width; check mark draws 300 ms; holds 3.2 s (6 s if failed), then the island returns to rest.

jobs.purpose: Parallel background jobs: a count in the bar, up to 4 rows in the hover peek.
jobs.useWhen: When 2+ agent jobs run at once (research, drafting, booking).
jobs.streaming: Count ticks with the tick sound; rows 110 ms apart in the peek; finished jobs leave with exit.

plan.purpose: The research plan: the question, numbered steps, scope, and an approve/edit window before work starts.
plan.useWhen: First block of every deep-research job. The user can edit steps or sources; auto-starts after a countdown.
plan.streaming: Steps appear 110 ms apart; the countdown ring runs once; on approval the card reshapes into the live canvas.

example.question: Which EU e-bike brands grew fastest in 2025–26?

steps.title: Collect 2025 and 2026 revenue or unit sales
Check funding and press for growth signals

research.purpose: Live status of a research job: stage, counters, current step, budget used.
research.useWhen: Pinned at the top of the research canvas and mirrored in the notch bar.
research.streaming: Counters roll (250 ms) as events arrive; stage chip crossfades; a thin progress bar eases with the reshape spring.

sourcefeed.purpose: Sources as they are found and read (favicon, title, site, state, relevance).
sourcefeed.useWhen: During research, so the user sees what the agent is looking at; collapses to a count when done.
sourcefeed.streaming: New sources slide in at the top, 110 ms apart (max 3 per second); state dot changes found → reading → read/used/skipped.

finding.purpose: One claim the research supports, with confidence and citation chips.
finding.useWhen: Key findings as they are established; later merged into the report.
finding.streaming: Pops in with the arrival spring; citation chips appear 60 ms apart; 'disputed' findings get a warn edge.

example.claim: Cowboy's 2025 unit sales grew about 40% year on year

evidence.purpose: A table of data extracted from sources, with a citation on every row (and optionally every cell).
evidence.useWhen: Numbers pulled from many sources: prices, revenues, specs, dates. Feeds charts and comparisons by $ref.
evidence.streaming: Rows draw in as they are extracted (110 ms); cells with conflicting sources show a small warning dot.

outline.purpose: The report's table of contents with each section's writing state.
outline.useWhen: While the report is being written, and as navigation in the final report.
outline.streaming: Sections tick from pending → writing (shimmer) → done; clicking scrolls to the section.

filters.purpose: Facets that filter or sort other blocks locally (tables, evidence, comparison, chart, gallery, map).
filters.useWhen: Final interactive reports with more than ~10 rows or several categories.
filters.streaming: Appears with the report; changing a facet re-filters targets in one frame (rows leave with exit, enter with the row reveal).

taskplan.purpose: A proposed split of a big goal into parallel agent jobs, with what each job may touch, approved once as a batch.
taskplan.useWhen: When one request becomes 3+ jobs ('we launch tomorrow, here are 100 issues').
taskplan.streaming: Groups appear 110 ms apart; the side-effect summary appears last; the approve button is enabled only when the summary has arrived.

example.summary: 8 jobs cover 100 issues. 2 jobs send or post publicly; you'll approve those before they go out.

taskgrid.purpose: Live list or grid of parallel jobs: icon, title, current step, status chip; finished jobs expand into a one-line result card.
taskgrid.useWhen: While 2+ jobs run. Pinned beside the work (a rail) or as a full grid.
taskgrid.streaming: Rows enter 80–110 ms apart; status chips crossfade; a finishing row expands with the reshape spring into a result card; older results compact back to a checked row.

goalbar.purpose: A slim bar naming the goal and the few numbers the brain found that matter for it (e.g. 47 asked · 31 customers · 52% of revenue · 2 promised).
goalbar.useWhen: Top of a brain-driven answer or plan, before any action. 2–5 metrics.
goalbar.streaming: Bar drops in (arrival spring); each metric ticks in as it is established, counting up over 750 ms, in step with the voice.

quote.purpose: A sourced quote callout: what someone said, where and when, with an optional tag (Promised, Asked, Complaint).
quote.useWhen: Evidence in their own words. Max 3 per answer; each must point at a real source record.
quote.streaming: Pops in next to its subject with the arrival spring; the source line fades in 150 ms after the quote.

provenance.purpose: A small 'why I know this' label: the fact, how many times and where it was seen, and when.
provenance.useWhen: Attach to a field, a row or a draft sentence the agent filled from the brain (target = block id, optional field).
provenance.streaming: Appears on hover or for ~2 s when the agent fills the field; never animates on its own afterwards.

graph.purpose: The brain as a graph: app sources (with counts) and entities linked by edges, with up to 3 highlighted paths.
graph.useWhen: Rarely: when the user asks how something was found, or as a 2–4 s 'looking' moment for a big goal. Never required to understand the answer.
graph.streaming: Nodes fade in by source, edges draw 300 ms each, highlighted path glows; collapses to the goalbar.

interrupt.purpose: A proactive banner the agent raises on its own: headline, impact chips, a risk pill, evidence rows with citations, one suggested action.
interrupt.useWhen: Only from the proactive engine, only above the interruption threshold, and only at a task boundary. Never in a normal reply.
interrupt.streaming: Shell drops from the top (≈ 0.7 s after the spoken cue), fills 400 ms later; evidence rows arrive in step with the voice; the action button comes last. Accepting turns it into agent tasks.

example.title: Lumen Health is about to churn

connectors.purpose: Onboarding connector cards: one per tool the user named, each with its scopes and live state; connected tools dock into the assistant pill.
connectors.useWhen: Setup by voice or text ('Gmail, Slack, HubSpot and Stripe'), or when a request needs a tool that isn't connected (use 'connect' for a single one).
connectors.streaming: A card pops in as each tool name is heard (about 0.5 s apart); states change in place; on success the cards fly into the pill and leave a CONNECTED icon row.

timeback.purpose: A small counter of time the agent saved today, with a breakdown on hover.
timeback.useWhen: Pinned near the assistant pill during a burst of tasks. Estimates only; label them as such.
timeback.streaming: Counts up (250 ms roll) each time a task resolves; never counts down.
